def: A way of writing names where words are joined with underscores and kept in lower case.
ex: customer_order_total

def: A way of writing names with no spaces, where each new word starts with a capital letter.
ex: customerOrderTotal

def: Three dots that show something is trailing off or left out. It can be typed as three full stops or as one special character.
ex: Wait... (three full stops) or Wait… (one ellipsis character)

def: Characters that take up no visible space, so you cannot see them, but they are still in the text and still cost tokens. They often arrive when you copy from a web page or a document.
ex: The word “price” can hold an invisible character between the r and the i (U+200B) and look exactly the same.

def: A space that looks normal but is a different character from the one on your space bar. It keeps two words on the same line, and word processors and web pages insert it automatically.
ex: 12 USD with a non-breaking space between 12 and USD looks identical to 12 USD with a normal space.

def: A long dash used to set off a phrase. It is a different character from the short hyphen on your keyboard.
ex: The plan — which is simple — works.

def: Quotation marks and apostrophes that curve, as word processors and many AI chat tools produce. Straight quotes are the plain ones on your keyboard.
ex: “yes” and it’s (curly) against "yes" and it's (straight)

def: The round bullet character used in lists, as opposed to a plain hyphen at the start of a line.
ex: • First item (bullet character) against - First item (hyphen)

def: Markdown is a way of marking up plain text. Hash signs make a heading and double asterisks make bold text. AI tools often add them to answers.
ex: ### Instructions and **Summarise** (Markdown) against Instructions: and Summarise (plain)

def: Rows of repeated symbols used to separate sections of text.
Labels wrapped in angle brackets that mark where a section starts and ends. Some prompt guides use them to separate instructions from data.
ex: <instructions>Summarise the text.</instructions>

def: The code around web page text. It is invisible when you view the page, but it comes along if you copy the page's source or save it as HTML.
ex:
Your order has shipped.

against Your order has shipped.

def: A long random identifier used by databases and apps to label a record.
The extra text after a question mark in a web address that records where a visitor came from. The page itself does not need it.
ex: https://example.com/shoes?utm_source=mail&utm_campaign=spring against https://example.com/shoes

def: JSON laid out with line breaks and indentation so people can read it. The same data can be written on one line with no extra spaces (minified).
JSON written on one line with no spaces or line breaks. It holds the same data as the readable version.
ex: {"id":1,"name":"Asha"}

def: Comma-separated values: plain text where each line is a row and commas separate the columns. Spreadsheets can export it.
ex:
id,name,role
1,Asha,admin
2,Ravi,editor

def: A readable data format that uses indentation and a colon after each name instead of brackets and quotes.
ex:
- id: 1
  name: Asha

def: A table written in plain text with vertical bars between the columns and a row of dashes under the headings.
Latin abbreviations. "e.g." means "for example" and "i.e." means "that is".
ex: Use a simple tone, e.g. friendly (for example), i.e. no jargon (that is).

def: Spaces or tabs at the start of a line that show structure, as in code or nested lists.
ex:
if x:
    return 1

def: The name of the tokenizer used by recent OpenAI models. A tokenizer is the rule set that splits text into tokens.
The name of an older OpenAI tokenizer, used by earlier models such as GPT-4. Counts often match o200k closely for English.
The rule set a model uses to split text into tokens. Different model families use different tokenizers, so the same text can have different counts.
A picture of a PDF page that the model looks at, either alongside the page's text or instead of it. Pictures are charged as image tokens, which is why a PDF can cost more than its words alone.
ex: One PDF page can arrive as two things: its text, and a picture of the page.

def: Pulling the typed text out of a file such as a PDF or a Word document, so that only the words are sent, without the page picture or the layout.
ex: A PDF page becomes plain text such as: Invoice 1042, total due 250.

def: The selectable text hidden inside most PDFs. A scan has none, because the page is only a picture of text.
ex: If you can highlight individual words with your cursor, the PDF has a text layer.

def: Optical character recognition: software that reads a picture of text and turns it into typed text. It can misread letters and digits, so check names and numbers afterwards.
ex: A scanned 1,000 can come back as 1.000 or l,000.

def: Searching a large file for the few passages that match your question and sending only those to the model, instead of the whole file.
ex: Asked about the refund window, the app pulls the refund section, not the whole 200-page manual.
